title: Bondy — Router / WAMP
description: Per-node router internals, WAMP sessions & messaging, HTTP gateway, and registry RIB routing.

panels.title: Router internals — RPC, listeners, jobs & limits
RPC promises in flight
panels.description: Pending calls/invocations awaiting a yield or error. Rising = callee saturation.

panels.title: Listener saturation
panels.description: Active vs max connections per ranch listener. Listeners with an unlimited max are absent.

panels.title: Partisan connections
panels.description: Connection-pool depth per peer and per channel (deeper than the connected/not-connected matrix).

panels.title: RPC timeouts & rate-limit denials
panels.description: Evicted RPC promises (caller got a WAMP timeout) and inbound requests denied by the AV-1 rate limiter. Both should normally sit at zero.

panels.title: Rate limiter & OIDC state
panels.description: Live token buckets (keyspace growth / GC health) and pending OIDC login flows.

panels.title: Singleton mailbox depth
panels.description: message_queue_len of critical singletons; a backed-up bondy_event_manager delays ALL eventing and metrics.

panels.title: Active sessions
panels.description: Event-driven gauge, all selected nodes.

panels.title: Session close reasons
panels.description: Sessions closed per second by WAMP close reason URI. A spike of abnormal reasons (ping timeouts, errors) is the "why are my clients dropping" diagnostic.

panels.title: Drops / shed (5m)
panels.description: Messages/events Bondy declined to deliver in the last 5m (bondy_wamp_dropped_total: load shedding etc.). Non-zero means a WAMP feature is degrading under load — the NATS "slow consumers" analog.

panels.title: Sockets & connections
panels.description: WAMP transport sockets by transport (raw = TCP raw socket, ws = WebSocket) with error rates, plus HTTP-layer connections per ranch listener (plain HTTP has no per-connection Bondy process; ranch is its source of truth and includes pre-upgrade WS connections).

panels.title: Ping RTT (quantiles)
panels.description: Round-trip time of router-initiated transport pings, per transport (ws | raw). Client connectivity health as seen from the router.

panels.title: WAMP message mix
panels.description: WAMP messages routed per second, by message type. One query per type family: rate() drops __name__, so a multi-name regex selector collides ("vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset") — this panel was broken since authoring.

panels.title: Call latency
panels.description: Round trip from the dealer receiving CALL to the first RESULT/ERROR, all procedures.

panels.title: Callee vs router time (p95)

targets.expr: clamp_min(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(bondy_wamp_call_latency_milliseconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))) - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(bondy_wamp_invocation_latency_milliseconds_bucket{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))), 0)

panels.description: Latency attribution: call = full CALL round trip; callee = INVOCATION to YIELD leg (application execution + transport); router overhead = the difference (approximate — quantiles do not subtract exactly). Answers "is it Bondy or is it the callee?".

panels.title: In-flight invocations by procedure (top 10)
panels.description: Pending invocations per procedure, computed from the live promise store at scrape time (drift-free). Rising values mean that procedure's callee is saturating — the per-procedure consumer-lag analog.

panels.title: Dropped by reason
panels.description: bondy_wamp_dropped_total rate by reason and family (e.g. shed meta events under load). Should be zero.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: API Gateway requests per second by route template.

panels.title: Error rate by route (%)
panels.description: Share of requests per route answered with a 4xx/5xx class status.

panels.title: Request duration p95 by route
panels.description: API Gateway request duration p95 per route template.

panels.title: Registry RIB — routing summaries, retry & presence
Local RIB members (per node)
panels.description: Live local registry entries feeding each node's replicated routing summaries.

panels.title: Remote stub cells (per node, per type)
panels.description: Remote routing summary stubs held per node, by registry type. Under RIB read/write mode this is the whole remote routing view.

panels.title: RIB divergences (last sweep)
panels.description: Keys where routing summaries disagree with the ground truth, as of each node's last periodic consistency sweep. Anything non-zero that does not self-heal within a sweep interval deserves attention.

panels.title: Pre-invocation retries (rate, by outcome)
panels.description: Cluster CALLs re-routed after an owner-side completion miss: node = re-routed to another node, local = absorbed by a local registration, exhausted = the error was final. A sustained rate means the routing summaries are running stale.

panels.title: Owner-side completions (rate, by outcome)
panels.description: Node-addressed forwarded CALLs completed by the owner: ok = a live local registration was selected, miss = none left (the caller retries or fails).

panels.title: Damping suppressions (rate)
panels.description: Summary updates coalesced by the damping window (count/latest-only changes). Zero when registry.rib.damping is off.

panels.title: RIB divergences (now)
panels.description: Node-wide total of routing-summary divergences at the last sweep. Green means the RIB agrees with the ground truth everywhere.

panels.title: Delivery pipeline — flow pool & HELLO admission
Flow queue wait (p95/p99 by family)
panels.description: Time a task waited in a flow pool worker mailbox before executing. Ordered flows cannot convert queue depth into throughput — sustained growth here IS delivery latency for every event behind it.

panels.title: Flow task service time (p95 by family)
panels.description: Execution time of a flow pool task (relay ingress / bridge relay). Pool throughput is bounded by pool size / this duration; a p95 far above p50 under load is scheduler starvation, not slow work.

panels.title: HELLO handling duration (p50/p95)
panels.description: In-process time handling a WAMP HELLO on the connection process (realm lookup, auth context, session open up to the encoded WELCOME). Compare against client-observed welcome latency: a large difference is queueing before the HELLO is even picked up.

panels.title: Admission refusals & sheds (rate)
panels.description: admission/hello = the load regulator refusing HELLOs cheaply while busy (retryable ABORT — protects the data plane). shed/* = flow pool overload discarding work at-most-once. Sheds should be ZERO in steady state; admission refusals are the designed relief valve.

panels.title: Registry pattern-index CAS contention
panels.description: Ptrie write rounds lost to a concurrent writer (retried) and writes that exhausted the retry budget (an incident). All pattern writes of a realm CAS on one root per (type, policy) — a sustained retry rate here is the trigger for pattern-broadcast sharding (_design/REGISTRY_PARTITION_GRAIN.md). Zero when uncontended.

panels.title: PUBLISH match p95 (registry lookup)
panels.description: Time a PUBLISH spent finding matching subscriptions. Grows with subscription count and pattern breadth, NOT with fanout. A tail here is a registry problem.

panels.title: PUBLISH fanout p95 (delivery + relay egress)
panels.description: Time a PUBLISH spent delivering: a send per local subscriber plus one relayed PUBLISH per peer node holding one. A tail here is delivery cost, not lookup.

panels.title: Relay-ingress mailbox depth p95
panels.description: Flow-pool worker mailbox depth at dequeue, RELAY INGRESS only — these tasks arrive from a peer with no dispatch timestamp, so the queue-wait histogram records nothing for them. A flow is FIFO on its worker, so depth x service estimates the wait behind it. Sustained growth = cross-node delivery latency.
